It states that among both genders, acceptance of cosmetic surgery related to lower general body appreciation and higher BMI (with some gender-specific differences noted), but specific correlation coefficients are not provided in the text.
section_summary.evidence_source: As an initial examination of the correlates of acceptance of cosmetic surgery in Brazil, we computed bivariate correlations between the overall ACSS score, General body appreciation, actual-ideal body weight discrepancy (women only, M=1.07, SD=1.15), the four SATAQ-3 subscales, participant age, and BMI, for women and men separately. As can be seen in Table 4, among women, higher acceptance of cosmetic surgery scores were significantly correlated with lower General body appreciation ... and higher self-reported BMI. The same pattern of significant correlations was found among men, with the exception of the lack of a significant association between the overall ACSS scores and the Information subscale of the SATAQ-3.
